rationale: Enabling fuzzy matching must not stop exact terms matching.
A single deleted character matches at medium sensitivity.
A transposition does not match at medium sensitivity, even though a deletion does.

Pinned as current behaviour rather than as obviously correct: the edit-distance threshold and which edits count toward it are exactly what drifts between implementations, so the corpus has to state it explicitly.
Term matching is case-insensitive, so a term the document writes in lowercase is still found when the policy writes it with a capital.
The span reports the text as it appears in the document, not the casing of the term that matched it. A span has to index its own text for offsets and text to stay usable together.
Fuzzy matching on its own does not require a capital: a lowercase near miss still matches.

This is the control for surname/capitalized-negative-lowercase, which is the same text under a policy differing only in 'capitalized'. Read the two together: they show that the option, and not something else, decides the answer.

cases.text: seen by Dr Smith on Tuesday

expect.filtered_text: seen by Dr Smith on Tuesday

rationale: Fuzzy matching widens what counts as a match, not where the terms come from.

Terms given in the policy replace the bundled list rather than adding to it, so a name the policy does not list is not found. This is what makes the case portable: an implementation shipping a different word list gives the same answer.
